title: `ia validate` admits a `@check` that names an evaluator that is not built in, to bind it; every other reader but `ia preview` and `ia author` keeps strict admission
summary: Relaxed, structural check admission (plan amendments C15 and C21), used by the validate request and, as their own note says, by ia preview and ia author, which 2.0.0 did not have. Released behavior is that a `@check` whose check.implementation or check.runs names an id that is not a built-in evaluator is refused with IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN and is not admitted. That stays the default for every reader of the admitted graph: the nine machine routes (scope, context, select, get, records, resolve, search, traverse, report), every ia scope form, ia position, ia next, ia read, ia capture, ia host, ia project, ia doctor, the MCP door, ia-distribution's other commands, and db open, the Door and compliance evaluate called without the new option; a test answers the nine routes and ia scope over an unknown-runner fixture byte for byte as strict admission does. What changed: ia validate and ia-distribution validate now admit structurally, so such a check is admitted, reported in the Checks section and bound (unavailable when no host catalog lists the evaluator), and the same workspace that ia validate reports as admitted is still refused by every strict reader with IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN, which ia validate's summary states; a check naming two different evaluators (IA-COMP-CHECK-CONFLICT) or none (IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN) is still refused by both. @inventarch/compliance adds validateCheckStructure(node) and ReportOptions.checks ('strict', the default, or 'structural'); @inventarch/db adds OpenOptions.checks and ViewOptions.checks with the same values and the same default (a handle opened structural never uses the cache, and its preview drafts structurally too), and @inventarch/runtime's DoorOptions, which extends OpenOptions, therefore accepts them, while the Door the machine routes open stays strict; @inventarch/distribution adds SessionOptions.checks. Not compatible with 2.0.0 for a consumer that relied on ia validate or ia-distribution validate refusing an unknown evaluator: such a workspace now validates with exit 0 when nothing else is wrong.
